metadata.title: Watch these chip stocks for bargain buys after Nvidia’s post-reinstatement rally

content.text:
Investing.com -- Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia CEO on Nov 23, 2026, 11 days after he resigned, sparking a broad-based rally across battered chipmaking and artificial intelligence names on Monday.
Our AI stock portfolio is beating the S&P 500 by 118%. Discover the stocks we're buying and the opportunities we're watching next. Exclusive for Yahoo! Finance readers: 55% off for Black Friday, plus an extra 15% at checkout. Subscribe today! »
Nvidia jumped nearly 33%, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index surged 14%. But despite broad gains in the sector, most major chip names were still trading down over the past month, amid a storm of headwinds.
But recent losses made chip stocks appear attractive as bargain buys, although major risks-- from Nvidia and U.S. regulations-- still persisted.
Stop chasing stocks after they've already rallied. Find your next investment opportunity with AI stock picks, earnings insights, and market-moving news. Yahoo! Finance readers get an extra 15% off on top of the 55% off Black Friday price. Join today! »
Bargain List
Values are snapshots from the screen (U.S. semiconductors above $20B market cap, at least 15% below their 52-week highs) and may lag live prices.
Insights
-
Broadcom rose only 3% on Nov 23. It sits 36.7% below its high, so less of the rebound is priced in. It also shows 28.4% fair value upside.
-
Micron's 3.4x forward P/E may reflect peak-cycle earnings. Its 19% one-day gain shows how quickly sentiment can reverse.
-
Credo's 22.6% one-day jump and Marvell's 18.4% rise show short-covering moves. Those can fade if the hearings go badly.
-
Regulatory risk is not uniform. The probes target Nvidia directly. Export curbs and tighter equipment rules could reach the equipment makers (Teradyne, Applied Materials). China exposure has not been checked for those names.
-
Revisit after the hearings. Dec 1 and Dec 3 are the clearest near-term catalysts for the whole group.
Nvidia's Huang to testify before Congress
Lawmakers of both parties have criticized the reinstatement. Democrats will hold majorities in both chambers from January and have promised "wide-ranging" investigations. Read more
Other Risks on the Table
-
Legal probes: The SEC is examining whether Nvidia's disclosures misled investors. California's attorney general has served a subpoena. The Megaspeed export-control case has become a criminal matter. An independent-director committee is also still investigating. Read more
-
Export legislation: Bills could block Blackwell sales to China for at least 18 months. They are in final negotiation for a December defense package. China is already excluded from Nvidia's Q4 guidance, so the exposure is mainly legal. Read more
-
Macro: The Fed's early-December rate decision is a risk. The 10-year Treasury yield was near 4.93% in that Nov 23 commentary. Read more
-
Short covering: Daiwa's Yugo Tsuboi attributed part of the surge to short covering. He also cited uncertainty over data-centre regulations.
-
AI return on spending: Nvidia said on Nov 17 it would be "far more selective" about financing AI industry deals. The ROI question is still open.
-
Competition: AMD and Google are putting pressure on Nvidia, which matters for chip peers too.
Several of these sit upstream of the whole sector. A bad hearing could hit the screened names even though most of them aren't Nvidia.
